notes:
PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached and no hardware or real-engine run is claimed. The card's entry symbol humanoidverse.simulator.mujoco.mujoco:MuJoCo exists at humanoidverse/simulator/mujoco/mujoco.py:15; it needs a Hydra config, Torch, mujoco and a viewer, so this package does not import or run it. The card decision is family-config with helper MujocoDriver, and this package serves the card's models[0], humanoidverse/data/robots/g1/scene_29dof.xml, through MujocoDriver, so there is no deviation from the card. The scene includes g1_29dof_old.xml: its free base (7 qpos, 6 qvel) and 29 hinge joints (29 qpos, 29 qvel) give a world state of 36 qpos and 35 qvel values, and its actuator section has 29 motor actuators with explicit ctrlranges (hips and waist yaw -88 to 88, knees -139 to 139, ankles and waist roll/pitch -50 to 50, shoulders, elbows and wrist rolls -25 to 25, wrist pitch/yaw -5 to 5; g1_29dof_old.xml:386-420). The bridge derives the cap.world.step.v1 ctrl limits from those model ranges and refuses an out-of-range element before writing data.ctrl. cap.world.reset.v1 runs mj_resetData + mj_forward and restores the parsed model qpos0 (pelvis 0 0 0.793, identity quaternion); the reset seed is accepted and recorded but MuJoCo does not use it. The scene and the included model declare no <option timestep>; the fake uses a marked placeholder default of 2 ms, while the upstream simulator overwrites model.opt.timestep with 0.005 s after loading (mujoco.py:148) and its setup uses 1/fps (mujoco.py:57, fps 200 in mujoco.yaml:15); this package loads the MJCF directly, no Fact claims a timestep, and the fidelity gaps state the difference. MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed here (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is the package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py, declared as the class FakeMujoco. The stand-in parses the same MJCF (include expansion in memory, the free base, the 29 hinges, the 29 motors and their ctrlranges) and gives each actuated hinge a placeholder velocity proportional to its control value; it loads no STL mesh or texture, resolves no contact, inertia, gravity, constraint, damping or actuator dynamics, and does not implement mj_getState/mj_setState, so snapshot/restore uses the bridge's qpos/qvel/ctrl/time fallback. The fidelity gaps list every difference, and no trajectory was compared with the real engine. WARNINGS kept from the last gate run (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake backend is the package's stand-in for the mujoco library rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder, so native calls are not recorded and G7 has no fake surface to check; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, which are expected for simulator families. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. TESTS: test_driver.py keeps the required mhs.testing.check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds eight cases (model shape from the card scene, control-vector length, control-range refusal with zero effect, step advancing the integration state, reset to the model defaults, reset seed recorded without changing the model, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1. No site-limits.example.json is needed because no operator-required bound and no driver-declared Limit is present; the control envelope is derived from the model at run time. NOT COVERED: the STL meshes, contacts, friction, sensors and the upstream Hydra/Torch control loop, and no comparison with the real MuJoCo engine or a physical Unitree G1.
